name: Apollo 11
description: US astronauts became the first to perform a crewed lunar landing and return to Earth.

name: Hubble Space Telescope
description: Space-based observatory launched to study the universe, free from Earth's atmospheric distortion.

name: Mars 2020: Perseverance Rover
description: Landing Feb. 18, 2021 on Mars, Perseverance Rover collects samples of Martian rock to search for signs of ancient microbial life.
objective: Seek signs of ancient life; Collect samples of rock and regolith

name: Project Mercury
description: USA's first human spaceflight program that included 6 crewed flights piloted by 'The Mercury Seven' military test pilots. It was foundational stepping stone into space, establishing the critical engineering, global communication networks, and human physiological baselines required for further exploration.
objective: First human spaceflight program; Recover crew and spacecraft safely; Evaluate human performan in space; Orbit a crewed spaceraft

name: James Webb Space Telescope
description: Space telescope designed to study the early universe, galaxy formation, stars, and planetary systems. It orbits the Sun near Earth's second Lagrange point (L2).
objective: Study the early universe and the formation of stars and planetary systems

name: Kepler / K2
description: Space telescope that searched for planets orbiting distant stars and expanded its observations during the K2 mission. It discovered thousands of exoplanets and candidates.

name: Spitzer Space Telescope
description: Space telescope that observed the universe in infrared light, studying objects ranging from nearby planets and stars to distant galaxies. It revealed Saturn's wispy rings and the first telescope to detect light from an exoplanet, and the first known star system with seven Earth-sized exoplanets.

name: Spirit
description: Uncovered strong evidence that Mars was once a much wetter planet, studying the history of climate and water in places where conditions may have once been favorable to life. Travelled 5 miles and operated for 6 years, more than 25 times its original intended lifetime.
objective: Investigate evidence of past water on Mars; Mars surface exploration

name: Voyager 1
description: The farthest spacecraft from Earth, Voyager 1 flew by Jupiter and Saturn making discoveries of new moons and Saturns new ring before crossing into interstellar space in August 2012. It continues to return data on the interstellar environment on an extended mission to reach one light-day away from Earth, more than 49 years in mission.
objective: Explore Jupiter and Saturn; Study the outer solar system; Investigate interstellar space

name: Voyager 2
description: The only spacecraft to visit all four giant planets: Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune at close range. It entered interstellar space - the second to do so after Voyager 1 - in December 2018 and continues to study the boundary of the Sun's influence.
target: Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune, Interstellar Space
objective: Explore the giant planets; Study the heliosphere and interstellar space

name: Cassini-Huygens
description: A NASA-ESA-Italian Space Agency mission that orbited Saturn for 13 years and delivered the Huygens probe to the moon Titan. It revealed Enceladus's global ocean and hydrothermal activity, Titan's methane seas, and detailed structure of Saturn's rings.
objective: Study Saturn, its rings, moons, and magnetosphere; Land the Huygens probe on Titan

name: New Horizons
description: The first spacecraft to explore Pluto up close, flying by the dwarf planet and its moons on July 14, 2015. It later flew by Arrokoth - becoming the most distant object explored upclose, in the Kuiper Belt - massive, ring-shaped region of icy objects and dwarf planets just beyond Neptune - on January 1, 2019, and continues studying the Kuiper Belt.
target: Outer edge of solar system, Pluto, Kuiper Belt
objective: Perform the first close exploration of Pluto and its moons; Study Kuiper Belt objects

name: Mars Science Laboratory: Curiosity Rover
description: Part of the Mars Science Laboratory mission, Curiosity landed in Gale Crater on August 6, 2012. It investigates whether Mars ever had conditions capable of supporting microbial life and analyzes Martian rock, soil, and atmosphere.
objective: Determine if Mars was ever able to support microbial life; Study Martian geology and climate

name: Opportunity Rover
description: Twin rover to Spirit, Opportunity landed in Meridiani Planum in January 2004 and found mineral evidence that Mars once had liquid water. It operated for nearly 15 years, far exceeding its planned 90-day mission. Opportunity ran for 28 miles before falling silent.
objective: Investigate evidence of past water on Mars; Explore Martian geology

name: Juno
description: Juno entered orbit around Jupiter on July 4, 2016, becoming the first spacecraft to peer beneath Jupiter's dense clouds. It aims to understand the planet's origin and evolution. It maps the magentic and gravitational fields. It studies the atmosphere, magnetosphere, and structures.

name: OSIRIS-REx
description: The first U.S. mission to collect a sample from a near-Earth asteroid. OSIRIS-REx rendezvoused with asteroid Bennu, collected rock and dust in 2020, and returned the sample capsule to Earth in September 2023. Scientists hope to reveal whether asteroids that collided with Earth billions of years ago, delivered water and other ingredients for life on Earth
objective: Collect and return a sample of asteroid Bennu, Study the origins of the solar system

name: Parker Solar Probe
description: The first spacecraft to fly through the Sun's corona, its upper atmosphere, in 2021. Parker studies the solar wind, coronal heating, and energetic particles while orbiting closer to the Sun than any prior spacecraft.
objective: Study the Sun's corona and solar wind; Trace how energy and heat move through the solar atmosphere

name: Artemis I
description: The first flight test of NASA's Space Launch System rocket and Orion spacecraft. The uncrewed mission traveled around the Moon and back to Earth, demonstrating systems needed for future crewed lunar exploration and beyond.
objective: Test SLS and Orion for deep-space human exploration; Demonstrate capability to return to the Moon
